title: DSWD: P23B in UPLIFT aid distributed to beneficiaries
summary: The Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) on Thursday said that it has distributed more than P23 billion in Unified Package for Livelihoods, Industry, Food, and Transport (UPLIFT) aid.

blocks.text: The Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) on Thursday said that it has distributed more than P23 billion in Unified Package for Livelihoods, Industry, Food, and Transport (UPLIFT) aid.
The UPLIFT program is the government’s welfare response to people affected by the ongoing crisis in the Middle East, which drove global prices to increase and contributed to faster inflation rates.
“Nasa mahigit P23 billion ang ating napamahagi doon sa mga UPLIFT beneficiaries,” DSWD spokesperson Assistant Secretary Irene Dumlao said on the Bagong Pilipinas Ngayon public briefing.
(More than P23 billion has been distributed to the UPLIFT beneficiaries.)

The UPLIFT beneficiaries are divided into three groups, Dumlao explained. Group 1 is for Pantawid Pamilyang Pilipino Program (4Ps) and Walang Gutom Kitchen beneficiaries, Group 2 is for people who are poor and non-poor, and Group 3 are beneficiaries who are SSS members but have a monthly income of less than P20,000.
For Group 1, Dumlao said that out of the 3.5 million qualified beneficiaries, 3.2 million households have received UPLIFT aid.
Meanwhile, Group 2 is composed of 2.5 million households, with 800,000 receiving the benefit. Dumlao said that this number is expected to go up, as distribution is ongoing through tranches.
Lastly, there are 1.3 million household beneficiaries under Group 3. Around 900,000 have been served as of the last tranche.
Dumlao reminded Group 2 beneficiaries that they only have until November 30 to update their information online, including their bank account.
While a manual cashout is still possible, Dumlao said that the agency encourage receiving UPLIFT aid through bank accounts or electronic wallets.
In terms of El Niño response, Dumlao said that more than P1 billion in cash aid, food packs and other forms of assistance have been distributed.
Most of this was through an emergency cash transfer, amounting to P913 million. —AOL, GMA News
